body:
FOUND 2026-08-10 chasing a CI flake to its root at Myk's direction, after two budget raises treated the symptom. MEASURED: test/store/archive.test.ts runs 0.7s on Linux and 12s NOMINAL on a healthy windows runner; three timeouts this week at 15s and 20s under load. The cost is the fixture's SETUP: append writes each delta open->write->fsyncSync->close->rename, synchronously, one at a time. 200 deltas x 30-80ms per Windows fsync = 10-16s of pure serial flushing. The purge sweep the test exists to pin is innocent.

EVERY REAL BATCH PAYS THIS: a federation pull landing N deltas into an archive-backed store flushes N times in series on the event loop.

THE FIX: overlap the per-delta writes with bounded concurrency (a small pool, ~16), preserving the per-file durability order EXACTLY — each file's bytes fsynced before its rename, temp cleaned on its own failure, first error still refuses loudly after the in-flight chunk settles. The promise does not move; only the wall clock. Purge's rmSync loop may get the same treatment if measurement says it matters (it did not this week).

RAILS: the existing frozen rail (test/store/archive.test.ts, T67) is the behavior rail and stays byte-identical — its 15s budget becomes comfortable headroom everywhere, which is the acceptance signal. A new perf-shaped rail is NOT wanted (a wall-clock assertion is a flake by construction; the honest measure is the CI timing trend).

CONTEXT for the wider worry (Myk, 2026-08-10): CI time must not grow unbounded. This ticket is the pattern's first instance: when a suite leans on a budget raise, ask what the code is doing per unit first. The vitest.config 20s default raise (erasure rails, sqlite) predates this lesson and may deserve the same look — a follow-up observation, not this ticket's scope.

WHO MERGES: self-merge on the ordinary bar — pure performance, no promise moves, the frozen rail is the regression net.
title: ArchiveBackend.append serializes one fsync per delta — a 200-delta batch pays 200 sequential disk flushes
